_readme: Every cell names a cached artifact or is null. null renders as an em-dash
in RESULTS_MATRIX.md with a footnote -- make_results_matrix.py never
interpolates, infers, or back-fills a missing number.

_maps_why: The convention tables that translate SHR's analytical vocabulary into
DCS's. They compose by backoff in eval_slm.py analysis(): the
convention map is tried first on the (lemma, cng) pair, the lemma map
second on the lemma alone. Both are built from TRAIN ids only and
build_lemma_map.py asserts dev/test membership is absent rather than
assuming it, so applying them at eval is not leakage.
They rewrite lemma and cng, never form, so S must be identical with and
without them. Any S movement between the two variants is a bug.
eval_slm.py applies them to cuSHR AND its ORACLE, never to --pred-jsonl:
ByT5 emits DCS conventions natively and needs no translation.

g95_heldout.label: g95 held-out (no surface reference)
g95_heldout.note: Out-of-domain by text, not by lattice source: every sentence still comes from an SHR graphml. No surface segmentation gold exists outside the published 4,200, so S / P / R / F1 / PM are unmeasurable here by construction, not merely unmeasured.

_note: cands/kbest are here only to produce the recall@K curve out to 64.
Verified they do not perturb the top-1 ladder: with and without them
anchors. The reranker cell below is deliberately LEFT at kbest 32:
reranking over 64 candidates instead of 32 is a different experiment
and would move its 91.98, which is not what filling in a column means.

why: The CPU decoder is not a different system: same biaffine weights,
same lattice, same top-1 Viterbi. Week 10 established the GPU top-1
is digit-identical to it, and k4_bench_F_k64_checked.csv re-confirms
it here with score_mismatch = count_mismatch = 0 over all 119,503
sentences. So its accuracy row IS the cushr_gpu_top1 row; only
throughput differs. Stated here rather than copied silently, so a
reader can see it is an asserted identity, not a second measurement.
NOTE: cpu_bench.csv's own precision/recall/f1 are node-level over the
whole 119,503-sentence corpus and are NOT the surface-level numbers
measured on the 4,200. Do not put those in this table.

_why: ByT5's own SIGHUM figure, cited beside the run we did ourselves.
These are NOT the same system configuration and the gap is large:
93.83 reported vs 81.38 measured. Their number comes from a model
FINE-TUNED ON SIGHUM, which learned SIGHUM's compound convention;
ours is the off-the-shelf chronbmm/sanskrit5-multitask checkpoint,
which learned DCS's. See PAPER_COMPARISON.md:347-351 -- of ByT5's
errors against this reference only 0.2% over-generate, so the S
column understates their system rather than measuring it badly.
Reporting our 81.38 alone would understate ByT5 by ~12 points.

published.citation: Nehrdich, Hellwig et al., *One Model is All You Need: ByT5-Sanskrit, a Unified Model for Sanskrit NLP Tasks*, Findings of EMNLP 2024, arXiv:2409.13920, Table 3 (SIGHUM column).
published.split_note: This is a SIGHUM figure and so is comparable in principle, but it is a **different configuration from the one we ran**: their model was fine-tuned on SIGHUM (99k samples) while ours is the released multitask checkpoint used off the shelf. The 12-point gap against our measured 81.38 is mostly that, not a reproduction failure. Their Hackathon figure is 94.29.
published.levels_corpus: DIFFERENT CORPUS -- Table 7, `Sen` column: a DCS April-2024 split (601,403 sentences, 8,398 test), not SIGHUM. Their test split also excludes reconstructed forms and is 'strongly biased towards Vedic texts' (their §5.5). Read this row for category alignment, never as a SIGHUM result. The `Par` column is excluded deliberately: it feeds pseudo-paragraphs of up to 512 characters, a different input granularity from our per-sentence decode.
published._verified: Read directly from Tables 3 and 7 of the PDF on 2026-09-08.

published.citation: Sandhan, Singha, Rao, Samanta, Behera and Goyal, *TransLIST: A Transformer-Based Linguistically Informed Sanskrit Tokenizer*, Findings of EMNLP 2022, arXiv:2210.11753, Table 1 (SIGHUM column).
published.split_note: Measured on the published SIGHUM test split, which overlaps ours by 97.02% (4,075 of 4,200 sentences; see PAPER_COMPARISON.md), so this is a comparison across near-identical rather than identical data. Their Hackathon column reads 97.78 / 97.44 / 97.61 / 85.47 and is a different dataset -- do not mix the two.
published._verified: Read directly from Table 1 of the PDF on 2026-09-08, not transcribed from a secondary source.
